description.p: Chippy shows your Dreame robot vacuum’s map with its rooms and where the robot is while it cleans, lets you pick the rooms to clean and start, pause or send the robot home. Sign in once with your Xiaomi account, by password or by scanning a QR code with the Xiaomi Home app; the session is kept in the GNOME keyring.
Edit the robot’s map too: draw no-go and no-mop zones and virtual walls, rename rooms, give each room its own suction, mopping and passes, set the cleaning order, and merge or split rooms.

Chippy can keep watching in the background and notify you when cleaning finishes or the robot needs help, and an optional top-bar extension puts the robot’s status and controls one click away. It is tested with the Dreame r2209 (Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X10); other Dreame models are experimental.
A small polish to map selection.

ul.li: Double-clicking a room to fit the map no longer makes its highlight flicker: the room switches back at once while the map zooms out
While the robot cleans, it now drives across the map to each new position instead of jumping there
Selected rooms fade to their highlight, and double-clicking the map eases back to the whole map
Pages cross-fade, and in edit mode the sidebar fades to the edit panel while the map tools slide in
All of this follows the system Animations setting
The robot stores each room’s mopping on a different scale than its general setting; Chippy now reads and writes it correctly, matching the Xiaomi Home app

Before this fix, the map editor showed each room’s mopping one level too high and saved it one level too low, and room cleaning from Chippy 0.1.3 used the misread level. If you saved room settings with an earlier version, check them in the editor or the phone app

description.p: Room cleaning now follows each room’s own settings.

ul.li: With “Use room settings” on, rooms you clean from Chippy get the passes, suction and mopping stored on the robot for each room, instead of one pass with the general levels
If the stored settings can’t be read, the clean still starts with the general levels

description.p: Safer map editing when the Xiaomi cloud is slow to show the robot’s new map.

ul.li: After a save, merge or split, editing pauses until the robot’s updated map arrives, so the next edit can’t start from the old map and undo the change; the pencil button explains the wait, and editing comes back after two minutes at most
Zones and walls the robot stores slightly rounded now count as saved straight away, instead of showing “the map will update shortly”
A room name that reaches the map late replaces Chippy’s temporary local copy as soon as it shows

description.p: Chippy now finds your robot again by itself when your router gives it a new IP address.

ul.li: When the robot stops answering, Chippy looks for it on your local network by its device ID, switches to its new address, reloads the map and remembers the address for next time
No Xiaomi cloud or sign-in is needed for this; it works while the robot is on the same network as your computer
The store description now mentions the map editor, live position and QR-code sign-in

description.p: The first release of Chippy, a GNOME app for Dreame robot vacuums.

ul.li: Live map: rooms with their areas, the dock, and the robot’s position and route while it cleans
Room cleaning: pick rooms on the map or in the list, choose suction and mopping, then start, pause, stop, send the robot home or make it play a sound
Map editor: no-go and no-mop zones, virtual walls, room names, per-room suction, mopping and passes, cleaning order, and room merge and split, all saved to the robot
Sign in with your Xiaomi password, or by scanning a QR code with the Xiaomi Home app for accounts that use Google, Facebook or Apple; robots shared with you are found too
Background alerts when a run finishes or the robot needs help, with readable names for Dreame fault codes
An optional GNOME Shell extension (GNOME 50 and 51) with status and quick controls in the top bar
